title: Diraq Finalizes $38 Million CHIPS R&D Award with U.S. Department of Commerce for Silicon Spin Quantum Chips - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Silicon spin-qubit developer Diraq has turned its May 2026 Letter of Intent into a definitive CHIPS R&D award of up to $38 million from the U.S. Department of Commerce, to fund U.S. fabrication, testing and research for its CMOS-compatible processors. Diraq was the only silicon spin-qubit company selected in this round. Its roadmap targets 150,000 physical / 1,000 logical qubits by 2029 and more than 2 million physical / 10,000 logical qubits by 2031, in a four-rack data-center footprint.

insights.claim: Diraq has finalized a funding agreement of up to $38 million with the U.S. Department of Commerce's CHIPS Research and Development Office under the CHIPS and Science Act, turning a May 2026 Letter of Intent into a definitive award.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: CHIPS quantum Letters of Intent are now becoming definitive awards. Watch the rest of the reported $2B Letter of Intent pool for similar conversions.
insights.locator: Silicon spin-qubit developer Diraq has finalized

insights.claim: Diraq was the only silicon spin-qubit company selected in this round of U.S. CHIPS R&D quantum funding.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Being the sole pick gives Diraq a policy-backed lead within the silicon spin-qubit modality.
insights.locator: The only silicon spin-qubit company selected

insights.claim: The CHIPS funding will speed up U.S.-based fabrication, testing and research infrastructure for Diraq's CMOS-compatible silicon quantum processors. It targets scaling bottlenecks including scalable Quantum Logic Units (QLUs), novel qubit arrays and global qubit control.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Because the chips are CMOS-compatible, U.S. semiconductor fab infrastructure could be reused for quantum chips, which fits the CHIPS policy aim of onshoring.
insights.locator: The funding will accelerate U.S.-based fabrication

insights.claim: Diraq is pairing its Australian scientific operations with expanded U.S. facilities in Palo Alto, Chicago, Los Angeles and Albuquerque.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: U.S. funding is pulling a foreign-origin quantum company's operations onto U.S. soil, which shows CHIPS money working as an onshoring tool.
insights.locator: The only silicon spin-qubit company selected

insights.claim: Diraq's roadmap targets 150,000 physical qubits supporting up to 1,000 logical qubits by 2029, and more than two million physical qubits with over 10,000 logical qubits by 2031, all within a compact four-rack data-center footprint.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: This is an aggressive, company-stated timeline that implies about 150 physical qubits per logical qubit. Use the 2029 milestone to judge whether Diraq delivers.
insights.locator: Designed to operate within a compact four-rack

insights.claim: Diraq has advanced to Stage C of DARPA's Quantum Benchmarking Initiative and has a commercial data-center deployment with Equinix.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: The DARPA Quantum Benchmarking Initiative Stage C and the Equinix deployment add outside validation beyond the CHIPS award.
insights.locator: Designed to operate within a compact four-rack
